blocks.text: Managing multiple client contexts in Chrome

Financial planners often work with many clients at once. You might have a custodian portal open for one client while updating a financial plan in another tab. Chrome profiles are the best way to handle this. Go to your profile icon in the top right of Chrome and select Add. Create a unique profile for each major client or project. This keeps your cookies and login sessions separate. You will never accidentally log into the wrong account again.
Essential Chrome shortcuts for Mac users

Keyboard shortcuts are the fastest way to move through your day. Press ⌘ + T to open a new tab. Press ⌘ + W to close your current tab. Use ⌘ + Option + Right Arrow to switch to the next tab. If you lose a tab, press ⌘ + Shift + T to reopen it. Memorizing these five commands will save you minutes every hour. You can view all shortcuts in Chrome by pressing ⌘ + /.

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you get work done. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you cannot find a specific setting in Chrome, ask Lazur to point it out. It draws a circle around the menu item. If you need to perform a multi-step task, ask Lazur to guide you. It will walk you through each click one by one.

You spend a lot of time typing notes into your CRM. Hold fn to dictate text directly into any field. Lazur formats your speech into clean text. This is much faster than typing long client summaries. You can also use clipboard slots to store common phrases. Use these for standard email replies or meeting summaries.

Security is mandatory for financial planners. Regularly clear your browsing data to protect client information. Go to Chrome > Settings > Privacy and security > Clear browsing data. Choose a time range and click Clear data. You should also check your extension list. Remove any extension you do not recognize. Go to Chrome > Window > Extensions to see what is active.

When you need to research investment options, use Lazur for research tasks. It runs in its own Chrome tabs and gathers information for you. It then gives you a summary report. This keeps your main browser window clean. You can focus on the analysis while Lazur handles the background work.

Most advisors spend 12 to 15 hours per week on client onboarding. By using Chrome profiles and keyboard shortcuts, you can reduce this time significantly. Focus on keeping your workspace tidy. Close tabs you are not using. Use a tab manager if you have too many open. This reduces memory usage and keeps your Mac fast.

blocks.text: If you find Chrome is running slowly, check your task manager. Press ⇧ + Esc to see which tabs are using the most memory. You can end those processes directly. This is a quick fix for browser lag. Always ensure your macOS is up to date to keep Chrome running well.

The transition to a digital-first practice is hard. You have to balance compliance with efficiency. Start by automating small parts of your day. Use Lazur to set reminders for follow-ups. Ask it to open your CRM and your calendar at the same time. These small actions add up over the week.

Keep your workspace clear of clutter. If you have too many browser windows, use Mission Control to organize them. Press Control + Up Arrow to see all your open windows. Drag windows to different desktops to keep your work separate. This simple step helps you stay focused on one client at a time.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Chrome for me?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not click buttons or edit files for you. It guides you one step at a time or points at things on your screen.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my client data?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not store your screen content or audio. It processes information only while you hold the shortcut and does not use it to train AI models.

faq.question: Is Chrome the best browser for financial planners on Mac?
faq.answer: Chrome is widely used because of its extensive extension ecosystem and compatibility with most financial planning web apps. However, you should choose the browser that best fits your firm's security requirements.

faq.question: How do I speed up Chrome on my Mac?
faq.answer: You can clear your browsing data, remove unnecessary extensions, and use the built-in task manager (Shift + Esc) to close heavy tabs.
